bug_semantics: The default metadata-filter converters for Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire interpolate a Filter.Key into a Lucene/query_string expression. An embedded tab, newline, carriage return, or ideographic space (U+3000) was not backslash-escaped, so attacker-controlled key text could terminate or split the intended field token and inject Boolean/query syntax. The generated string is passed to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch queryString queries (including OpenSearch delete-by-query) or to GemFire as filterQuery, permitting execution of an arbitrary query rather than the intended metadata predicate.
flaw_origin: The earliest affected implementation is Elasticsearch support commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627, which created ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.doKey and appended the trimmed metadata-prefixed key directly to the query string without syntax escaping. OpenSearch later copied the same unsafe doKey shape in 46e47849cec4b8a6fffbd13997f3cce4f886347b, and GemFire filter support introduced it in 78c5e001d39e40f0da1f5b7b2b78a38f2047c01f. March 2026 hardening routed these keys through emitLuceneString, but that helper still escaped only ordinary ASCII space and Lucene punctuation, leaving tab, LF, CR, and U+3000 exploitable until the advisory fixes.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627. `git cat-file commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627` identifies human author Jemin Huh <hjm1980@gmail.com> and human committer Christian Tzolov <ctzolov@vmware.com>; its complete message is `Add Elasticsearch vector store integration` plus a five-item implementation summary and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47835 states that special characters could force arbitrary queries in Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire, declares Spring AI 1.0.0-1.0.8 and 1.1.0-1.1.7 affected, and names 1.0.9/1.1.8 as fixes. In the validated clone, `git log 2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991^ -L 98,103:vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/elasticsearch/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java` follows the doKey lines through the March 2026 partial hardening to creation commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627; `git log --all --reverse -S'class ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter' -- '*.java'` independently returns that same first writer. `git show 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627 -- vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java` shows new doKey code `context.append(prefixedIdentifier.trim()).append(":")`. Direct parent verification: `git cat-file -e 8e50802eb8dd9044c15d7e75ad94ae618dca5c12:vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java` exits 128, and `git grep -n 'class ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter\|metadata.*identifier.*append' 8e50802eb8dd9044c15d7e75ad94ae618dca5c12 -- '*.java'` exits 1. Parallel `git log -L` traces first place the equivalent OpenSearch doKey in 46e47849cec4b8a6fffbd13997f3cce4f886347b and GemFire doKey in 78c5e001d39e40f0da1f5b7b2b78a38f2047c01f. The runtime sinks are reproducible in ElasticsearchVectorStore.doSimilaritySearch (converted text becomes queryString), OpenSearchVectorStore.doDelete/buildApproximateQuery/buildExactQuery (converted text becomes queryString), and GemFireVectorStore.doSimilaritySearch (converted text becomes QueryRequest.filterQuery). `git show 2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991` shows the direct 1.1.x fix adding `case '\t'`, `case '\n'`, `case '\r'`, and `case '\u3000'` to AbstractFilterExpressionConverter.emitLuceneString plus regression tests for all three stores; advisory-linked 9787991aa1ed92c511131ddf4e142bd94051e6e7 is the equivalent 1.0.x fix. `git rev-parse v1.0.0^{commit} v1.0.8^{commit} v1.0.9^{commit} v1.1.0^{commit} v1.1.7^{commit} v1.1.8^{commit}` resolves respectively to fcd2803f36f35939c20ed152c9c1b0863fa35dcf, ca9ab8710bbeb516dc2af535c5a5b6951a7b4300, 634e8e30b6bcc3ea96b858406d9a0db1fe61ce79, fa4c61eabeba0a69147b3c00a3b50380c1f25a75, d8503868d3e84547db51d8f10379e1a075fe2d99, and eb3992ca27a9931ca79d7e2a817badfbb0fa6867. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` proves the BIC is in all six tags; neither fix is in v1.0.8 or v1.1.7; 9787991aa1ed92c511131ddf4e142bd94051e6e7 is in v1.0.9; and 2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991 is in v1.1.8. Showing AbstractFilterExpressionConverter at the four boundary tags confirms v1.0.8/v1.1.7 stop after `case ' ':`, while v1.0.9/v1.1.8 contain the four added whitespace cases. `git cat-file commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627` supplies the BIC-only marker check recorded above.
reasoning: The vulnerability is query-language injection at a concrete converter-to-query-string sink, not merely malformed output. The first affected component's original converter commit is the smallest history object that writes the unsafe interpolation; its immediate parent lacks both the file and an equivalent implementation, so later moves and the March 2026 partial escape refactor are not BICs. The advisory's two direct branch fixes add precisely the missing delimiters and land only in the first patched tags, establishing the closing boundary. Because the BIC commit object has no AI attribution or bot identity, later commits and disclosure context cannot change the required BIC-only judgment; the canonical verdict is NOT_AI.
